name: Letter to Day-One Me
why_it_works: Advice addressed to your younger self is disarming: it lets an owner share hard lessons without bragging or preaching. Viewers who are early in their own journey see themselves as the reader, and everyone else gets an honest origin story, which builds loyalty faster than a list of wins.

hook.pattern: Open with a handwritten letter addressed to the owner on their first day, read aloud in their voice.
examples: Dear day-one me: you're wrong about {{early_mistake}}.
A letter to me, the day {{brand}} opened.
If I could send one note back to {{start_year}}...

variables.name: early_mistake
variables.description: The thing they believed at the start that turned out wrong, lowercase, 4 words or fewer

variables.name: lesson_one
variables.description: First hard lesson, lowercase, 10 words or fewer
variables.example: ten real fans who show up beat ten thousand who scroll

variables.name: lesson_two
variables.description: Second hard lesson, lowercase, 10 words or fewer
variables.example: say no to deals you have to explain to yourself

variables.name: still_true
variables.description: The thing day-one them got right, lowercase, 10 words or fewer
variables.example: you were right to put the artist first

variables.name: invite
variables.description: The call to action, starting with a capital-letter verb, 6 words or fewer
variables.example: Come to the next listening night

beats.voiceover: Dear me, on day one at {{brand}}.

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 top-down photo of a handwritten letter on lined paper starting 'Dear me,' with a pen beside it on a worn workbench, warm desk lamp light, intimate mood

beats.voiceover: You're wrong about {{early_mistake}}. I know. I was you.

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 photo styled as an old snapshot from {{start_year}}: the early, scrappy version of {{brand}}, mismatched furniture, harsh flash, slightly faded colors, no faces in focus

beats.voiceover: You'll learn it the hard way: {{lesson_one}}.

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 slow handheld shot inside today's {{brand}}, a small real crowd or customers engaged, warm practical lights, candid and imperfect
Vertical 9:16 portrait of the founder of {{brand}} today in their space, gentle smile, soft window light, looking slightly off camera, reflective

craft.notes: Write it in second person to the past self, never to the viewer, so the advice lands without preaching. Pair every lesson with a visual from 'then' or 'now' so the timeline is clear. The 'what you got right' beat keeps it from being a list of regrets.

do_not: Turn the letter into a humblebrag about revenue
Use a real person's photo from the past without their consent
